security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD RISC-V kernel has zero V-extension support: no vtype CSR save/restore in context switch, no SSTATUS_VS bit tracking, no vector fields in PCB. If rudimentary V support is added without preserving the full vtype register (including the new altfmt bit at position 8), a context switch between a process using altfmt=1 (BF16 mode) and one expecting altfmt=0 (FP16 mode) would corrupt floating-point vector computation semantics for the victim process. Additionally, any kernel code that read-modify-writes vtype field-by-field (vsew, vlmul, vta, vma) without preserving bit 8 would silently clear altfmt.
security_spec.summary: Zvfbfa adds altfmt bit (bit 8) to vtype CSR; FreeBSD currently has no V-extension support at all (no vtype in PCB/mcontext/context-switch), so any future V support addition must preserve the full vtype register including altfmt to prevent BF16/FP16 format corruption across context switches

findings.finding: SSTATUS_VS (bits 9-10, vector context state tracking) is not defined. Only SSTATUS_FS (bits 13-14 for float) and SSTATUS_XS (bits 15-16 for user extensions) exist. Without SSTATUS_VS, the kernel cannot track whether a process has dirty vector state, making lazy/on-demand vector context switching impossible.
findings.snippet:
#define SSTATUS_FS_SHIFT  13
#define SSTATUS_FS_MASK   (0x3 << SSTATUS_FS_SHIFT)
#define SSTATUS_XS_SHIFT  15
#define SSTATUS_XS_MASK   (0x3 << SSTATUS_XS_SHIFT)
/* SSTATUS_VS (bits 9-10) NOT DEFINED */

spec_citations.excerpt: vtype register layout: bits 2:0=vlmul, 5:3=vsew, 6=vta, 7=vma, 8+ reserved, XLEN-1=vill. Currently no altfmt bit defined in the base V-extension spec at this reference version.

findings.finding: No vector CSR addresses are defined. Missing: CSR_VSTART (0x008), CSR_VXSAT (0x009), CSR_VXRM (0x00A), CSR_VCSR (0x00F), CSR_VL (0xC20), CSR_VTYPE (0xC21), CSR_VLENB (0xC22). The kernel has no ability to read or write vtype or any vector control/status registers.
findings.snippet:
#define CSR_FFLAGS 0x1
#define CSR_FRM 0x2
#define CSR_FCSR 0x3
/* CSR_VSTART 0x008, CSR_VTYPE 0xC21, etc. NOT DEFINED */
#define CSR_CYCLE 0xc00

findings.finding: struct pcb has no vector state fields. Only floating-point state is stored: pcb_x[32][2] (32×128-bit F registers) and pcb_fcsr. Missing: vector register storage (v0-v31, each VLEN bits wide), vtype, vl, vstart, vcsr, vlenb. A process's vector execution context cannot be saved or restored across context switches.

spec_citations.excerpt: vtype register layout table: vill (XLEN-1), reserved (XLEN-2:8), vma (7), vta (6), vsew[2:0] (5:3), vlmul[2:0] (2:0). Full vtype must be saved/restored to preserve altfmt if Zvfbfa is supported.

findings.finding: Context switch path (cpu_switch, cpu_throw, savectx) only saves/restores floating-point state via __fpe_state_save and __fpe_state_load macros. No vector save/restore macros exist. If V-extension support were added, context switching between processes using altfmt=1 (BF16) and altfmt=0 (FP16) would corrupt vector computation semantics because vtype is not preserved.

set_fpregs() and set_fpcontext() manipulate SSTATUS_FS via &= ~SSTATUS_FS_MASK / |= SSTATUS_FS_CLEAN field-by-field mask-and-set pattern. If vector support were added mimicking this pattern for vtype (e.g., vtype &= ~mask; vtype |= new_fields), the altfmt bit (in the reserved range bits 8+) would be silently cleared whenever only vsew/vlmul/vta/vma fields are updated, corrupting BF16 mode for the process.

spec_citations.excerpt: vtype bits XLEN-2:8 are reserved. If Zvfbfa repurposes a reserved bit as altfmt, field-by-field mask-and-set operations that only preserve bits 0-7 would corrupt altfmt.

findings.finding: ISA string parser does not recognize 'v' (vector) extension. Handles single-letter extensions 'a','b','c','d','f','h','i','m','s','x','z' and multi-letter 'z*' extensions, but no 'v'. HWCAP_ISA_V is also not defined in sys/riscv/include/elf.h. The kernel cannot detect or advertise V-extension capability to userspace.

Illegal instruction trap handler only checks for FPU lazy-enable (PCB_FP_STARTED flag, fpe_state_clear(), SSTATUS_FS_CLEAN). No vector lazy-enable path exists. A userspace process executing a vector instruction on hardware with V-extension would take an illegal-instruction trap with no kernel handler to enable VS state, preventing any V-extension use.

Only floating-point state management functions exist (fpe_enable, fpe_disable, fpe_store, fpe_restore, fpe_state_save, fpe_state_clear). No corresponding vector state management API (v_enable, v_disable, v_store, v_restore, v_state_save, v_state_clear). The save area alloc/free/reset infrastructure (fpu_save_area_alloc/free/reset) has no vector equivalent.

bhyve VMM (virtual machine monitor) only saves/restores floating-point context (fpe_state_save, fpe_restore, fpe_store) for guest VCPUs. No vector state save/restore for guests. A guest OS using V-extension (including Zvfbfa BF16) would have its vector state corrupted across VM exits, as vtype (including altfmt) is not preserved.

/* fpe_state_save / fpe_restore / fpe_store for guest FPE context */
/* No vector state save/restore for guest VCPUs */
